selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Proxy-mode WebSocket frame inspection across AV, IPS, DLP and File Filter
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Proxy-mode protocol-options profile enables WebSocket parsing so UTM engines inspect messages inside the upgraded tunnel; it is distinct from HTTP proxy request-length enforcement.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client HTTP CONNECT/HTTPS -> proxy TLS inspection -> HTTP Upgrade handshake -> WebSocket frames -> AV/IPS/DLP/File Filter verdict -> allow or block; proxy URI-size validation can fail before the WebSocket stream is established.
selected_candidates.failure_class: WebSocket not inspected because profile/policy is flow mode or status disabled; proxy denies long URI with HTTP 414; TLS inspection or protocol parsing mismatch.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Forward-traffic log shows UTM allowed versus proxy denied; browser shows 414; proxy debug identifies URI too long; WebSocket handshake and UTM logs show whether frames reached inspection.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use proxy inspection mode; enable WebSocket in the protocol-options profile; attach the intended AV/IPS/DLP/File Filter profiles; separately tune explicit-proxy max-request-length only when logs prove URI-length rejection.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish UTM WebSocket frame inspection from explicit-proxy URI-length denial; identify the stage at which 414 occurs and what the log proves.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client -> explicit proxy/TLS inspection -> HTTP Upgrade -> WebSocket frame parser -> parallel AV/IPS/DLP/File Filter engines; pre-handshake URI-length rejection side branch.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No WebSocket frame-inspection lesson or equivalent proxy URI-stage lesson appears in the 330 historical records; selected from FortiOS 8.0 New Features Guide.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiGuard package version pinning and controlled rollback
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager FDS package repository exposes a preferred To Be Deployed Version per FortiGuard package; Just Set Preferred Version prevents future rollout beyond the chosen version, while Downgrade actively returns managed devices already on newer package versions.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FDS download and repository update -> administrator selects package version -> preferred version stored -> managed FortiGate requests package from local FDS -> device receives pinned version; optional downgrade pushes older package to devices already beyond it.
selected_candidates.failure_class: FDS download/HTTPS proxy failure, AVIPS service disabled, unsupported TLS/proxy mode, entitlement or package missing, mistaken firmware-version rollback instead of signature-package pinning.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiGuard Packages receive status and version dates; diagnose fmupdate update-status fds; FDS debug shows TLS protocol alert or connect error; proxy logs show 503/504; device package version compared with preferred version.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Verify AVIPS service and contract, DNS/FDS reachability and proxy tunnel mode; populate package repository; select preferred version; choose downgrade only when devices must be actively reverted; monitor receive and device install state.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Differentiate preferred-version pinning from forced downgrade and firmware upgrade; identify FDS connectivity prerequisites before changing package version.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGuard FDS -> FortiManager package repository -> preferred-version selector -> managed FortiGate fleet; separate pin-only and downgrade rollout branches.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No FortiGuard package version pinning/rollback mechanism in the 330 historical records; distinct from firmware-template sequencing and policy package installs.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Playbook editor node-level debugging, replay and partial execution
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 playbook editor adds step-by-step debug, task-output inspection, replay with new input, partial execution from a selected node, Jinja control flow and Branch/Wait/Compare/Switch nodes.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Alert/event trigger -> playbook input mapping -> ordered task graph -> connector/API action -> downstream decision; debug pauses at each node, replay injects changed input, partial run starts from a selected node.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Wrong source-device mapping, alert-handler scope limitation, malformed input or Jinja expression, inactive connector, branch condition mismatch, task failure hidden by end-to-end run.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Per-node input/output and execution state; connector status; trigger payload fields such as groupby1/epip; task result and replay comparison.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Separate trigger selection from playbook execution; map the source event to the target FortiGate explicitly; run step-by-step debug; inspect the first incorrect node; replay from that node with corrected input; verify connector active state.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish event-trigger/alert-handler scope from cross-device playbook action; choose the earliest node to inspect and when partial replay is safe.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiWeb alert -> FortiAnalyzer playbook trigger -> input mapping -> node-by-node debug lane -> FortiGate connector action -> branch/wait/compare outcome; replay bypass lane.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The editor's debug/replay/partial-run execution model is distinct from historical on-demand playbook triggering and automation-stitch/alert-handler topics.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Auto-network and automatic ISL topology formation versus CAPWAP FortiLink discovery
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch auto-network/auto-ISL creates LACP-active inter-switch trunks and applies management-VLAN defaults; FortiLink CAPWAP access-controller discovery is a separate control-plane advertisement that can still cause remote adoption.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Factory reset/standalone switch -> LLDP and auto-network detect neighbor -> physical inter-switch links join auto-ISL LAG -> mgmt VLAN 4094/native VLAN and trust/edge defaults apply; separate CAPWAP discovery packets can advertise the switch to a remote FortiGate.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Unexpected remote FortiLink adoption across L2 extension, VLAN deletion, port/hostname rewrite, loss of standalone config; disabling auto-ISL alone leaves CAPWAP discovery active.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: auto-network/auto-isl and auto-fortilink-discovery values; LLDP neighbor and LACP actor/partner state; CAPWAP discovery traffic; FortiGate switch-controller adoption event; management VLAN 4094.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Choose intended standalone or FortiLink mode; disable auto-network/auto-isl and auto-fortilink-discovery as appropriate; disable AC discovery with config switch-controller global set ac-discovery-type disable when remote adoption must be prevented; review LLDP profile.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish automatic ISL trunk formation from CAPWAP controller discovery; determine why disabling auto-ISL did not prevent adoption.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two standalone FortiSwitches auto-form an LACP ISL and management VLAN; separate CAPWAP discovery broadcast crosses L2 extension to remote FortiGate; AC-discovery disable gate.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The historical records cover MCLAG/LACP/EVPN and FortiLink adoption, but not the distinct auto-network plus CAPWAP-discovery split and its L2-extended adoption failure.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: RADIUS authentication survivability for previously authenticated 802.1X clients
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiGate/FortiAP caches a RADIUS-provided credential hash for a previously authenticated PEAP client and uses it for local reauthentication during RADIUS unavailability; new or expired clients still need RADIUS.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: 802.1X/EAP-PEAP -> RADIUS Access-Request/Challenge/Accept -> credential-hash attribute and server certificate trust cached -> RADIUS outage -> known client reauthenticates locally until cache timeout -> RADIUS recovery or cache expiry returns normal flow.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Missing hash attribute, untrusted RADIUS CA/server certificate, survivability disabled, cache expired, or false assumption that a new client can authenticate during outage.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: RADIUS Access-Accept contains Fortinet-AS-Credential-Hash or Cisco-AVPair AS-Credential-Hash; PEAP client identity and cache age; wpad station logs; RADIUS packet capture; server connectivity test.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable survivability on the correct enterprise SSID; configure the hash attribute on RADIUS; import root CA and server certificate; set a bounded cache interval; test known and new clients separately and verify RADIUS recovery.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish cached-client reauthentication from new-client authentication; interpret a failed direct RADIUS test during an outage without assuming the cache is broken.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client -> FortiAP/FortiGate 802.1X authenticator -> RADIUS server with credential-hash return; outage branch to local cache with timeout gate; new-client deny branch.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No credential-hash caching or RADIUS outage survivability mechanism appears in the historical wireless lessons; distinct from RadSec transport security.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Kerberos authentication support for FortiNAC Manager and Control Application identities
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds Kerberos for admin and user authentication on FNAC-CA and admin authentication on FNAC-M; directory configuration carries the NetBIOS/domain identity used for Kerberos, distinct from LDAP attribute lookup and Winbind MSCHAPv2 trust.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User/admin enters domain identity -> FortiNAC directory maps realm/NetBIOS context -> KDC issues service ticket -> FortiNAC validates ticket and applies role; LDAP lookup retrieves user/group attributes on a separate path.
selected_candidates.failure_class: NetBIOS/realm mismatch, KDC DNS or time skew, missing domain trust/SPN, LDAP lookup succeeds but Kerberos ticket authentication fails, or Winbind/MSCHAPv2 path confused with admin login.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Directory configuration and NetBIOS name; domain/KDC DNS and clock; Kerberos authentication logs; LDAP user lookup success; Winbind trust state and MSCHAPv2 test result.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Align the configured NetBIOS/domain identity with the AD domain; verify KDC discovery, time synchronization and service identity; test Kerberos login separately from LDAP search and Winbind/MSCHAPv2 authentication.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Separate Kerberos admin/user authentication from LDAP attribute lookup and Winbind-backed MSCHAPv2; interpret LDAP success with Kerberos failure.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin/user -> FNAC-M/FNAC-CA directory identity -> KDC ticket exchange -> role decision; parallel LDAP attribute lookup and separate Winbind/MSCHAPv2 branch.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The 330 historical records include FortiNAC-F Winbind/MSCHAPv2 domain join but not FortiNAC 9.4 Kerberos for FNAC-M/CA admin and user authentication.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Microsoft Entra ID as a native FortiNAC-F authentication source for 802.1X and captive portal
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Service Connector authenticates users against Microsoft Entra ID for local RADIUS TTLS-PAP, captive portal and certificate-based workflows, then maps synchronized remote groups to NAC roles; TTLS-PAP flow does not support MFA.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Supplicant -> AP/switch -> FortiGate RADIUS client -> FortiNAC-F local RADIUS/TLS -> Entra ID connector token/authentication -> user/group mapping -> Access-Accept and network role; remote-group poll is a separate sync path.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Connector credentials/permissions or token flow fail, TTLS-PAP MFA assumption, RADIUS TLS trust mismatch, user authenticates but remote group import fails due 255-character description limit.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Service Connector status and poll output; local RADIUS Access-Request/Accept/Reject; group import debug AzureADApplicationInterface; output.master SQL Data too long for column description; role mapping result.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Validate Entra app registration and connector permissions; choose supported auth flow and do not expect MFA with TTLS-PAP; validate RADIUS certificate chain; shorten group descriptions to 255 characters; re-poll and verify group-to-role mapping separately from user authentication.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Differentiate successful user authentication from failed remote-group synchronization; identify TTLS-PAP MFA limitation and 255-character group description boundary.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Supplicant -> AP/switch -> FortiGate RADIUS -> FortiNAC-F service connector -> Entra ID; side remote-group sync -> NAC role map -> Access-Accept.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The historical FortiNAC-F lessons cover SAML SSO, Winbind and device tags but not Entra ID as the direct RADIUS/captive-portal authentication source; the selected focus is TTLS-PAP and group synchronization, not the earlier FortiAuthenticator SCEP/EAP-TLS flow.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Active-passive HA priority override: fail back to healthy preferred node or minimize failovers
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator HA election combines node priority with monitored-interface health and a stability period; Priority Override selects either favoring a recovered healthy high-priority node or minimizing additional failovers.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Active/standby heartbeat and state sync -> monitored interfaces evaluated -> stability timer -> priority override policy selects active node -> authentication services move; node-specific gateway configuration remains a separate per-node routing state.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Unexpected failback, repeated role changes, interface-count precedence misunderstood, stability timer too short, or authentication node active but default route wrong after reboot.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: HA role/priority, monitored-interface count and state, stability timer, peer heartbeat/sync, authentication request destination, per-node static route and node-specific gateway.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Choose the failover policy deliberately; monitor only service-critical interfaces; set a stability interval appropriate to link flaps; verify sync before failback; inspect node-specific gateway and static route independently after role changes.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Differentiate interface-health precedence from priority, and HA role selection from node-specific routing; select the intended failback policy.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FortiAuthenticator nodes with heartbeat/state sync, monitored-interface and stability gates, two priority-override decision paths, and independent per-node gateway routes.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No FortiAuthenticator HA priority-override/failback policy appears in the historical inventory; distinct from FortiNAC-F HA and other product HA mechanisms.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Just-in-Time Windows privilege elevation using PowerShell checkout/check-in scripts over WinRM
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Secret checkout runs a PowerShell script over WinRM to add the mapped user to a privileged local/domain group; check-in runs a paired script to remove membership; script failure warns but does not block checkout/check-in.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User checks out secret -> FortiPAM resolves target privileged or associated-secret credential -> WinRM remote session -> Add-LocalGroupMember/Add-ADGroupMember -> user signs out/in to refresh token -> check-in -> Remove-LocalGroupMember/Remove-ADGroupMember -> sign out/in again.
selected_candidates.failure_class: WinRM unavailable, privileged credential resolution fails, user variable empty due Launch secrets with PAM credentials, script command missing Member argument, check-in script not executed, or existing logon token retains elevation.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Get-Service WinRM returns Running; Test-WSMan reaches target; Secret Event & Video shows script stderr; Add-LocalGroupMember missing Member indicates empty variable; Get-LocalGroupMember shows membership before/after.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable and test WinRM; verify target privileged account or associated secret; correct variable scope by using explicit secret username or associated-secret context; validate both scripts; verify membership and require sign-out/in after elevation and de-elevation.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Interpret missing Member argument as variable-resolution failure rather than group-policy denial; distinguish successful checkout from successful script execution and token refresh.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: User checkout/check-in -> FortiPAM secret and credential resolver -> WinRM -> PowerShell add/remove group membership; OS token refresh gates before and after.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The historical FortiPAM topics cover rotation, checkout, approvals, launchers and migration but not reversible JIT group membership through paired WinRM scripts.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Policy-based and file-based Event Tagging as post-parse enrichment
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Event Tagging applies ordered policy-based rules and CSV file-based mappings to Collector-parsed events; later matching rules can overwrite earlier tags, and changes require separate Apply operations.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Raw event -> parser/normalization -> policy-based tags top-to-bottom -> file-based tags top-to-bottom -> enriched event -> rule/report evaluation; custom parser collisions occur before tag enrichment.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Wrong tag rule order, file mapping mismatch, saved-but-not-applied rules, later rule overwrites, attempt to repair parser field collision with a tag, reserved system attribute overwritten.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Raw event and parsed Event Name/Event Type; tag policy order and Apply state; Collector event attributes before/after; CSV key match; parser test versus live event.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Validate parser output first; create policy-based or CSV file-based tags on stable parsed keys; order rules intentionally; apply both policy and file-based changes separately; avoid reserved/system-managed fields.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish parser normalization from post-parse tags; predict last-match overwrite and identify why a saved rule has no effect until Apply.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Raw source -> Collector parser -> ordered policy tag rules -> ordered CSV tag rules -> enriched event -> analytics/rules; parser-fault side branch before tagging.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No FortiSIEM Event Pipeline Event Tagging lesson appears in the 330 records; distinct from parser authoring and incident-rule tags.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Agent-based ZTNA destination objects using IP ranges, subnets and port lists
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE agent-based ZTNA destination objects can match literal IPs, ranges/CIDR and optional port lists/ranges; destination type controls whether endpoint DNS resolution is required.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiClient agent intercepts app traffic -> destination object match by host/range and port -> FortiSASE policy/PoP steering -> private access path -> SPA/FortiGate gateway -> private application; FQDN match adds DNS proxy resolution before policy match.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Feature-version or FortiClient version gate, incorrect CIDR/port definition, FQDN resolution delay over IPv6, destination object not referenced by policy, private route/gateway unavailable.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiSASE Feature/Mature version; FortiClient build; destination object type and port list; endpoint DNS query timing; FortiClient log 'Block IPV6 DNS query'; private access gateway route and policy hit.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable the required Feature version and FortiClient 7.2.8+; define the narrowest valid range/CIDR and port set; use literal IP objects where DNS is not required; validate policy and private path separately.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Differentiate destination-object matching from DNS resolution; choose IP range versus FQDN when IPv6 DNS proxy delay is observed; preserve least-privilege port scope.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint FortiClient -> destination object match (CIDR/range/ports or FQDN/DNS) -> FortiSASE policy/PoP -> private gateway -> application; DNS timeout side branch.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: The inventory includes agentless ZTNA and split DNS, but not agent-based destination IP range/subnet/port matching; the new match object is a distinct policy primitive.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiCloud SD-WAN Overlay-as-a-Service transaction, rollback and spoke verification
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS controller communicates with the FortiGate OaaS agent over FGFM, validates and compares target configuration, applies it as a transaction, and rolls back orchestrated changes if any step fails.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS portal task -> FGFM management tunnel -> FortiGate OaaS agent validates target/current config -> transaction applies SD-WAN zones, members, policies and overlay settings -> commit/sync or rollback -> spoke traffic continues -> get oaas status reports version/task/error.
selected_candidates.failure_class: OaaS license absent/expired, FGFM tunnel or FortiCloud reachability failure, pre-existing SD-WAN service ID 1 conflict, invalid target config, BGP/IPsec/route/SLA not converged after deployment.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: System > FortiGuard SWOS entitlement; diagnose test update info; get oaas status configuration version/sync status/task ID/error; show system sdwan; BGP summary and IPsec tunnel state.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: License every participating FortiGate; verify FGFM and FortiCloud reachability; migrate conflicting default service rule ID 1 before OaaS deployment; inspect get oaas status; verify IPsec, BGP, routes, SLAs and policy after commit; retry only after correcting the reported conflict.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish portal task failure from successful local config sync; identify default SD-WAN service ID 1 conflict and use transaction/rollback status correctly.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiCloud OaaS controller -> FGFM tunnel -> FortiGate OaaS agent -> compare/validate -> transaction apply -> commit or rollback; parallel spoke data plane and verification path.
selected_candidates.selection_reason: No OaaS controller/agent transaction or rollback lesson appears in the historical records; distinct from FortiManager overlay templates and Fabric Overlay Orchestrator IPAM.
